meaning:
διπλόος
(poët., διπλός, whence corp. -ότερον), -όη, -όον (-οῦ, -ῆ, -οῦν) [in LXX for כָּפַל, מִשְׁנֶה, and cognates ;]
twofold, double: 1Ti.5:17, Rev.18:6; διπλότιρον, in twofold measure: Mat.23:15.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much…
Let the elders who rule well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those who labor in the word and in teaching.
Return to her just as she returned, and repay her double as she did, and according to her works. In the cup which she mixed, mix to her double.
